title: request-graph-driven-prefix-merger-and-kv-snapshot-journal
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a request-graph-driven prefix merging system with lightweight KV snapshot journals to deduplicate prefix KV across concurrent and interleaved requests. The goal is to reduce GPU resident KV footprint and cross-request duplication while preserving low tail latency for streaming/continuous-batching workloads. This ticket covers signature design, in-memory journal format, merge-time heuristics, allocator hooks for slab compaction, integration with microbatch routing, and a staged rollout plan with fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end microbenchmark: 20-35% reduction in GPU KV memory for mixed short/long prompt workload without regressing p95 token latency by >5%
No correctness regressions: generated tokens must match baseline for canonical prompt set (deterministic model); unit tests for snapshot/merge semantics added
Operational observability: dashboards showing dedupe hit rate, net slab reclaim, merge cost (ms), and fallback rate
Safe rollout plan: feature gate with percent rollout, automatic degrade to existing cache when merge conflicts exceed threshold
implementation_notes: Build a lightweight request graph at the front of the serving pipeline that records prefix ancestry and equivalence hints across requests in the active batching window

Compute a canonical prefix fingerprint using a two-stage scheme: (1) cheap locality-preserving hash on token ids + template id, (2) optional content-addressed SHA256 when hash collision risk high or for long prefixes

Maintain an append-only in-process KV snapshot journal (per-worker) that records candidate prefix insertions during microbatch assembly; journal entries are probabilistically deduplicated before committing to the GPU slab

Introduce a commit step that tries to atomically attach shared KV slices to multiple requests; if commit fails for some request due to concurrent eviction, fall back to per-request local KV with corrective reconciler
Add GPU slab allocator hooks: tag slabs with live-reference counts derived from merged prefix attachments and a reuse-heat score used by eviction/compaction

Merge heuristics: prefer merging prefixes with high reuse-heat, similar token-length distributions, and compatible lifetime windows (i.e., expected residency through remaining generation tokens), limiting cross-model merges to verified compatible architectures
Expose lightweight telemetry: dedupe_attempts, dedupe_successes, journal_size_bytes, commit_latency_ms, slab_reclaimed_bytes
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Merge/commit can add latency spikes on microbatch critical path. Mitigation: make journal commit asynchronous with a synchronous optimistic path that serves from local KV until commit confirmation; also enforce a p99 commit-time budget with enforced fallback
Risk: Fingerprint collisions leading to incorrect shared KV usage. Mitigation: two-stage fingerprint with optional definitive SHA-based verification for high-risk or long prefixes
Risk: Increased memory churn from speculative merges. Mitigation: tight TTL policies on speculative attachments and a background compaction pass that reclaims low-heat merged slabs
Risk: Multi-tenant safety (cross-tenant dedupe). Mitigation: tenant id embedded in fingerprint namespace and strict RBAC check before sharing
testing_plan: Unit tests for journal append/dedupe/commit semantics with deterministic mock allocator
Integration tests with continuous-batching simulator covering interleaved requests and rollback scenarios
Benchmarks: run existing microbench harness (short-heavy, long-light, mixed) and compare memory, cost-per-token, and latency p50/p95/p99
Chaos tests: force commit failures and eviction during commit to validate fallback and reconciler correctness
rollout_plan: Feature gated at node level behind 'request_graph_prefix_merge' flag
Start with 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% across low-traffic tenants over 4 weeks, monitor dedupe success and latency
Enable automatic disable if commit_latency_p99 > 2x baseline or dedupe_failure_rate > 5% over 15m window
Post-rollout: enable background compaction and knob for aggressive slab reclamation
